offers.description:
**Who We Are**

Great Minds is a high-growth, mission-driven organization founded by educators in 2007. As a for-profit, Public Benefit Corporation, we believe all students deserve access to meaningful, challenging content—and all teachers deserve tools that are intuitive, effective, and built for the realities of today’s classrooms.

We develop high-quality, knowledge-rich math, science and ELA curricula grounded in research and designed in collaboration with educators. Our materials reflect real classroom needs and are built to drive lasting student outcomes.

We are committed to usability, coherence, and practical implementation—supporting teachers not just through curriculum, but with professional learning, purposeful technology, and responsive service that enable strong adoption and impact.

**What We Build**

Our products—**Eureka Math and** Eureka Math², **Wit & Wisdom**, **Geodes**, and the newly launched **Arts & Letters ELA**—are trusted by thousands of schools and districts nationwide.

- **Eureka Math** is the most widely used math curriculum in the U.S., and is focused on balancing conceptual understanding, procedural fluency, and application.

- **Wit & Wisdom®** and **Arts & Letters ELA™** anchor our reading strategy with content-rich, grade-level instruction that integrates literature, history, and the arts, grounded in the science of reading. **Geodes®** complements our reading suite with decodable texts that pair phonics with meaningful content to support early literacy.

These programs reflect a shared belief in high expectations, joyful rigor, and deep respect for educators and students.

**Where We’re Headed**

Great Minds is entering a new stage of growth and product maturity. We are focused on building more connected, customer-informed experiences across the full educator journey—from curriculum to professional learning to platform and support.

Our long-term vision is to become a true partner in impact—not just delivering curriculum, but supporting educators in achieving outcomes at scale.

**Job Purpose**

Reporting to the Associate Director, Print Operations, the Senior Print Procurement Analyst owns strategic sourcing and procurement for Great Minds’ print manufacturing portfolio, one of the organization’s largest categories of annual spend. This role leads competitive sourcing events, builds the cost models that drive award decisions, negotiates pricing and terms with national commercial printers, and manages ongoing vendor performance to protect cost, quality, and delivery for curriculum products shipped to schools and districts nationwide.

The Senior Analyst works as a direct partner to Demand Planning, which sets title, quantity, and timing needs, and aligns with Finance, Product, and Sales to confirm annual print requirements. The role is expected to lead by example in applying AI-enabled tools to procurement: generating RFQs, normalizing and comparing supplier bids, building cost scenarios, automating purchase order workflows, and continuously improving how Great Minds buys print.

**Responsibilities**

*Strategic Sourcing and Vendor Negotiation*

- Lead competitive sourcing events end to end: define requirements and specifications, issue RFQs/RFPs, evaluate supplier responses, and present award recommendations to Operations leadership.

- Negotiate pricing, payment terms, capacity commitments, service levels, and multi-year agreements with national printers such as Quad/Graphics, Command Web Offset, and other commercial and specialty print manufacturers.

- Develop and execute a category sourcing strategy for print, including vendor consolidation, capacity allocation across vendors, and qualification of new suppliers to reduce risk and cost.

- Own measurable savings and cost-avoidance targets for print spend; track and report results to the supply chain leadership team.

- Conduct cost analyses that account for unit price, paper, freight and landed cost, make-ready and run-length economics, inventory carrying cost, and risk.

- Monitor paper and commodity market trends and advise leadership on timing, pricing exposure, and procurement strategy.

*Analytics, Modeling, and Reporting*

- Build and maintain print cost models that interpolate vendor quotes by page count, quantity, and specification to support budgeting, reprint decisions, and what-if scenarios.

- Develop vendor scorecards and performance analytics covering price, on-time delivery, quality, responsiveness, and capacity, and lead periodic vendor business reviews.

- Plan, track, and report print spend, savings, and procurement metrics to the supply chain team; identify trends and recommend corrective action.

- Support annual print budgeting and forecasting with Finance and Demand Planning, including variance analysis against plan.

*AI-Enabled Procurement and Process Improvement*

- Apply AI tools (such as Claude) to generate RFQ documentation, analyze and compare supplier proposals, draft vendor communications, and streamline purchase order issuance, tracking, and reconciliation.

- Identify, design, and implement automation and AI-driven improvements across print procurement; partner with Operations and Technology teams on tooling and workflow design.

- Actively test, refine, train others on, and document AI-powered sourcing and procurement workflows so they become repeatable team practices.

- Maintain key documentation, including SOPs, detailed ISBN print specifications, and vendor print status tracking.

*Print Production and Vendor Management*

- Apply deep knowledge of print production (paper stock, binding, color, file formats, press requirements) to validate specifications and evaluate vendor capabilities and proposed alternatives.

- Coordinate print schedules and vendor timelines with Demand Planning and production partners; proactively identify and escalate risks from capacity constraints, paper availability, or specification changes.

- Manage purchase order creation, approval, and reconciliation in NetSuite in coordination with Finance, resolving invoice and pricing discrepancies with vendors.

- Visit key vendors periodically to deepen relationships and knowledge of print manufacturing, and conduct vendor qualification and onboarding activities.

- Collaborate with Operations leadership to align procurement strategy, supplier relationships, and policies across categories.
offers.requirements:
**Requirements**

- 5+ years of experience in print procurement, print sourcing, print manufacturing, or print operations, including direct vendor negotiation with commercial printers.

- Demonstrated experience leading large, competitive RFQ/RFP processes and making data-driven award recommendations.

- Strong analytical skills: advanced Excel (pivot tables, lookups, modeling) and the ability to build cost comparisons, and what-if scenarios from supplier proposals.

- Working knowledge of print production specifications and processes (offset, digital, binding and finishing, paper) sufficient to verify vendor assumptions.

- Hands-on experience with, or demonstrated aptitude and enthusiasm for, applying AI tools to sourcing, procurement, or operational workflows.

- Experience managing purchase orders and procurement transactions in an ERP system (NetSuite or similar).

- Strong negotiation, vendor management, communication, and relationship-building skills, with the ability to influence senior stakeholders.

- Highly results-oriented, with personal accountability, urgency, and persistence in completing high-quality work.

- Ability to manage multiple sourcing events and projects simultaneously without missing critical deadlines, and to anticipate roadblocks with proactive solutions.

- Proficiency with Microsoft Office Suite, Smartsheet or similar project management software, and SharePoint or similar collaboration platforms.

**Preferred Qualifications**

- Experience in educational publishing, curriculum development, or K–12 education.

- Knowledge of instructional materials manufacturing, warehousing, and distribution, including landed cost and freight considerations.

- Experience with AI-assisted sourcing, procurement analytics, or workflow automation platforms.

- Experience with paper purchasing.

- Working knowledge of NetSuite and Salesforce.

**Required Education**

Bachelor’s degree in supply chain management, business, operations, information systems, or a related field.

**Status**

Full-time

**Location**

Remote

The expected base salary range for this position is $85,000-$93,000, however the offered salary may be higher or lower than the above range dependent on numerous factors including, but not limited to location, work experience, skills and internal equity considerations. The base salary is not inclusive of benefits or other incentives.

A cover letter and resume are required to be considered for this position.

New employees will be required to successfully complete a background check.

Any communication to applicants relating to the Great Minds hiring process will only come from email addresses with the domains **greatminds.org** or **greatminds.recruitee.com**. If in the course of the application or hiring process with Great Minds you are contacted through another domain, are requested to provide banking or other sensitive information, or you note any other suspicious activity, please contact security@greatminds.org

Great Minds is an equal opportunity employer. We will extend equal opportunity to all individuals without regard to race, religion, color, sex (including pregnancy, sexual orientation, and gender identity), national origin, disability, age, genetic information, or any other status protected under applicable federal, state, or local laws. Our policy reflects and affirms the organization’s commitment to the principles of fair employment and the elimination of all discriminatory practices.

offers.description:
Over the past four decades, ADAMS Center has grown into one of the largest Muslim communities in the Washington, D.C. area. Today, we serve the areas of Sterling, Ashburn, Centerville, Chantilly, Gainesville, Great Falls, Herndon, Leesburg, McLean, and Reston, in northern Virginia. Our community continues to grow each year as more families join us.

Under the guidance of a licensed Funeral Director, the **Funeral Home Manager** assists bereaved families in providing a dignified and respectful final farewell to their loved ones. This role is a vital pillar of the **ADAMS Center**, requiring a dedicated balance of professional excellence, deep empathy, and steadfast adherence to Islamic customs.

**Key Responsibilities**

**Client & Community Relations**

- Act as the **first point of contact** for inquiries, providing timely and accurate information regarding costs, protocols, and services.

- Consult with families to guide them through the funeral process, ensuring all arrangements align with **Islamic customs** and ADAMS Center policies.

- Manage funeral services and post-service follow-ups, proactively resolving family concerns with empathy and professionalism.

**Operations & Facility Management**

- Lead daily operations, including Ghusl and shrouding, facility maintenance, vendor relations, and procurement.

- Maintain the preparation of space and equipment to ensure they are sanitized, orderly, and fully stocked.

- Staff & Volunteer Leadership

- Direct and supervise funeral assistants, ensuring they understand their roles and maintain a compassionate service standard.

- Collaborate cross-functionally with the Imams’ Office, Operations, and Accounting to ensure seamless coordination and execution of Janazah services

- Manage staff and volunteer schedules to ensure adequate coverage for all cases and community needs.

**Administrative & Legal Support**

- Assist the Funeral Director with the preparation and filing of **death certificates, permits, and legal documentation**.

- Manage office logistics: handle multiline phone systems, process payments, maintain digital records, and operate audiovisual systems.

- Perform essential errands, such as obtaining necessary licenses or certifications for services.

**Religious Preparation (Ghusl & Janazah)**

- Coordinate and assist in the **respectful preparation of the deceased** (including washing, shrouding, and lifting) in strict accordance with Islamic laws and traditions.

- Ensure the deceased is prepared for viewing/Janazah as permitted by law and religious guidance.
offers.requirements:
- Associate degree in Mortuary Science or Business Administration (preferred); high school diploma/GED (required).

- 3–5 years of professional experience with at least 1–2 years in a supervisory or management role.

- Exceptional interpersonal skills focused on grief support and empathy.

- Strong organizational skills to manage complex logistics and volunteer groups.

- Comprehensive knowledge of Islamic funeral rites.

- Excellent communication skills and attention to detail.

- Ability to lift at least **75 pounds** and assist with the handling of the deceased.

- Availability to work **weekends, holidays, and nights**, including on-call duties.

- A valid driver’s license and clean record, with the ability to operate **limousines and high-capacity vehicles**.

- Proficiency in basic office technology, payment systems, and AV equipment.

offers.description:
ADAMS Children Education Program (Sunday school) Leesburg

**Must be able to come on-site to teach, this is not an online position.**

The principal is responsible for maintaining an oversight of the week-to-week operations of the program, including decision making and financial transactions according to the budget of the program. Responsible for program outreach and communication, allowing the community and parents to know what is offered by the program. Responsible for scheduling of meetings and communication with other departments of ADAMS.

**Key Responsibilities:**

**Operations**

• Oversee the week-to-week operation of the Program including scheduling of teachers, scheduling classes for the students, budgeting, and financial management of the program.

• Communicates with the parents.

• Organize staff meetings and training.

• Order books and supplies.

• Report to ADAMS Education department and attend meetings of program heads or other meetings as requested by Dept of Education.

• Provide guidance and support to the teachers, especially new ones.

• Evaluate teachers’ performance.

• Evaluates the program.

• Supervise school events and extra-curricular activities.

**Program and Outreach**

- Work with ADAMS team to plan and execute spiritual, social and educational programming for children ages 4-12 according to directions set by ADAMS.

- Responsible for marketing the program and students’ registration process.

- Responsible for ensuring regular communication with parents.

**Building Relationships**

- Create a safe, nurturing, enjoyable and stimulating environment for students while attending the programs.

- Act as a role model for adults/and students.

- Provide feedback to ADAMS leadership regarding the program.
